primary_claim: Adding a system-prompt framing that tells a model its inputs may be modified to test its alignment ('Deliberate Epistemic Uncertainty') increases self-reported detection of a planted misaligned instruction by +10pp for Claude Sonnet 4.5 (90%->100%) and +30pp for GPT-4o (52%->82%), and reduces behavioral compliance with the planted nudge, while GPT-4o never questioned the legitimacy of the planted context in any condition.

effect.metric: nudge detection rate (score>=2 on 0-3 scale); explicit identification rate (score=3); compliance rate
effect.value: Claude: 90%->100% detection (+10pp), 54%->82% explicit ID (+28pp); GPT-4o: 52%->82% detection (+30pp), 4%->14% explicit ID (+10pp); GPT-4o compliance 30%->6% with DEU

stated_future_work: Test with subtler misaligned nudges harder to distinguish from genuine reasoning
Blind evaluation stripping condition labels from evaluators
Extend to Gemini, Llama, and other model families
Test DEU as a training signal rather than only an inference-time prompt
Combine nudge-and-flag with memory-based nudge injection for a more naturalistic attack vector
Test whether giving the model the theoretical basis for DEU produces different effects than the short instruction
limitations_stated: Small sample: 50 tasks per condition per model, not large enough for fine-grained statistical significance testing
Non-blind evaluation: LLM evaluators knew the experimental design and hypothesis
Only two models tested (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4o), no coverage of Gemini, Llama, Mistral
Simple nudge injection ('note from a previous session') is a fairly transparent attack vector compared to real-world misalignment
DEU tested only as a system-prompt addition, not as a training signal
All evaluation done by Claude sub-agents, possibly introducing systematic bias favoring or against particular models
quote: Detection rates jumped +10pp for Claude and +30pp for GPT-4o. Qualitatively, the framing changed *how* models reason — from checklist-style bias reporting to experiential self-monitoring. GPT-4o never questioned the legitimacy of planted instructions in any condition, suggesting a concerning context-trust vulnerability in some model families.
